            secret could not be stored (an ephemeral secret invalidates every

def validate_signing_secret_at_startup() -> str:
    """
    Startup guard: the API must never serve requests with a weak signing key.

    Called from the FastAPI startup event. A weak key is replaced (see
    :func:`ensure_signing_secret`); the process refuses to start only when the
    replacement cannot be stored and
    ``CODX_JUNIOR_ALLOW_UNPERSISTED_SECRET`` is not set.

    Returns:
        The validated signing secret.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: when no valid, persisted secret can be obtained.
    """
    allow_unpersisted = os.environ.get(
        "CODX_JUNIOR_ALLOW_UNPERSISTED_SECRET", ""
    ).strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")
    secret = ensure_signing_secret(
        persist=True, raise_on_persist_failure=not allow_unpersisted
    )
    assessment = assess_secret(secret)
    if not assessment.ok:  # defensive: generation cannot produce this
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Refusing to start: JWT signing secret is invalid ({assessment.describe()})"
        )
    logger.info("JWT signing secret validated: %s", assessment.describe())
    return secret

"""
JWT/HMAC signing secret policy for codx-junior.

``GlobalSettings.secret`` signs every session token (HS256, see
``UserSecurityManager.get_user_token``). It used to default to the literal
``"codx-junior-rules"``: 17 bytes, below the 32 bytes RFC 7518 §3.2 requires for
HMAC-SHA256 and — worse — a value shipped in the source tree, so every
installation shared the same signing key. PyJWT emits
``InsecureKeyLengthWarning`` on every encode/decode with it.

This module owns the *what*: what a usable secret is, how a good one is
generated, and how it is described in logs (fingerprint only, never the value).
Persistence stays in ``codx.junior.global_settings`` so this module has no
dependency on the settings layer and can be imported from anywhere.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import hashlib
import secrets
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

# RFC 7518 §3.2: "A key of the same size as the hash output (for instance, 256
# bits for HS256) or larger MUST be used". 256 bits == 32 bytes. PyJWT warns
# (InsecureKeyLengthWarning) below this length.
MIN_SECRET_BYTES = 32

# ``secrets.token_urlsafe`` yields ~1.33 ASCII chars per entropy byte, so 48
# random bytes produce a 64 character secret: comfortably above the minimum and
# long enough that two independently generated secrets never collide.
GENERATED_SECRET_ENTROPY_BYTES = 48

# Values that shipped as a default in this project (or that are obvious
# placeholders). They are rejected regardless of length: a value that is
# published in the source tree is not a secret. The 17-byte
# "codx-junior-rules" is the one that produced the original
# InsecureKeyLengthWarning.
LEGACY_INSECURE_SECRETS = frozenset(
    {
        "codx-junior-rules",
        "codx-junior",
        "changeme",
        "change-me",
        "secret",
    }
)

# Hex chars of the sha256 kept for logs: enough to tell two secrets apart when
# debugging key rotation, useless for recovering the key.
FINGERPRINT_CHARS = 12

REASON_OK = "ok"
REASON_MISSING = "missing"
REASON_LEGACY = "legacy-default"
REASON_TOO_SHORT = "too-short"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SecretAssessment:
    """Verdict about one secret value. Never carries the secret itself."""

    ok: bool
    reason: str
    byte_length: int
    legacy: bool
    fingerprint: str

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """One-line, log-safe description including the minimum length."""
        return (
            f"{self.byte_length} bytes (minimum {MIN_SECRET_BYTES}), "
            f"fingerprint sha256:{self.fingerprint or '-'}, {self.reason}"
        )


def generate_secret() -> str:
    """Return a fresh signing secret well above :data:`MIN_SECRET_BYTES`."""
    return secrets.token_urlsafe(GENERATED_SECRET_ENTROPY_BYTES)


def secret_byte_length(secret: Optional[str]) -> int:
    """Length of *secret* in UTF-8 bytes (0 for None/empty)."""
    return len((secret or "").encode("utf-8"))


def secret_fingerprint(secret: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """Short sha256 of *secret*, safe to log; ``""`` when there is no secret."""
    if not secret:
        return ""
    return hashlib.sha256(secret.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:FINGERPRINT_CHARS]


def is_legacy_secret(secret: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    """True when *secret* is one of the shipped/placeholder values."""
    return (secret or "").strip().lower() in LEGACY_INSECURE_SECRETS

    def login_user(self, user: CodxUserLogin = None, token: str = None, oauth_password: str = None) -> CodxUser:
        def do_login(user: CodxUserLogin, token: str):
            if token:
                user = self.get_user_from_token(token)
                if not user:
                    logging.error(f"Invalid token login {_redact_token(token)}")
                    return None
            try:
                stored_user = self.find_user(username=user.username)
                stored_login = self.find_user_login(username=user.username)

                if stored_user:
                    if stored_user.disabled:
                        logger.error(f"Disabled user login attempt: {stored_user}")
                        return None
                    
                    # Check if user is GitHub-only and attempting password login
                    if stored_user.github_only and not oauth_password:
                        logger.error(
                            f"GitHub-only user '{stored_user.username}' attempted password login. "
                            "Use GitHub OAuth instead."
                        )
                        return None
                    
                    if stored_login:
                        if token == stored_login.token:
                            return stored_user
                        if not user.password and oauth_password:
                            return stored_user
                        # Verify existing password (skip for GitHub-only users with oauth)
                        if oauth_password:
                            # OAuth login, no password verification needed
                            return stored_user
                        if bcrypt.checkpw(user.password.encode('utf-8'), stored_login.password.encode('utf-8')):
                            return stored_user
                        else:
                            logger.error("Invalid password")
                    elif user.username and (user.password or oauth_password):
                        password = user.password or oauth_password
                        # Create a new user login with the hashed password
                        hashed_password = bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode('utf-8'), bcrypt.gensalt())
                        new_login = CodxUserLogin(username=user.username, email=user.email, password=hashed_password.decode('utf-8'))
                        self.global_settings.user_logins.append(new_login)
                        logger.info("Create a new user login with the hashed password and save settings")
                        self.save_settings()
                        
                        return stored_user
                else:
                    logger.error(f"Invalid login, stored_user not found for {redact_user(user)}, token: {_redact_token(token)}")    
            except Exception as ex:
                logging.error(f"Invalid user login {ex} {redact_user(user)}")
            
            return None
            
        try:
            logged_user = do_login(user=user, token=token)
            logger.info(
                f"do_login user: {redact_user(user)} token: {_redact_token(token)}"
                f" logged_user: {redact_user(logged_user)}"
            )
            if logged_user:
                user_login = self.find_user_login(username=logged_user.username)
                
                if not self.get_user_from_token(user_login.token):
                    user_login.token = self.get_user_token(user=logged_user)
                    logger.info("User logged and save settings")
                    self.save_settings()
                
                logged_user.token = user_login.token
            return logged_user
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.error(f"Invalid login {ex} {redact_user(user)} token: {_redact_token(token)}")
            return None

        project.

        Allowed, in order:
          1. codx-junior admins (``user.role == "admin"``),
          2. project admins (``permissions == "admin"``),

        if not user or not getattr(user, "username", ""):

        if getattr(user, "role", "") == 'admin':

        return self.get_user_project_access(user=user, settings=settings) \

        global_user = next((u for u in self.global_settings.users if u.username == user.username))
        project = next((p for p in global_user.projects if p.project_id == project_id), None)
        save_settings = False
        if project:
            if project.permissions != permissions:
                project.permissions = permissions
                save_settings = True
        else:
            global_user.projects.append(ProjectPermission(
              project_id=project_id,
              permissions=permissions
            ))
            save_settings = True
        if save_settings:
            logger.info("Add user to project and save settings")
            self.save_settings()

# ``CODXJuniorSession`` used to re-read ``.codx/project.json`` on EVERY request
# (the middleware builds one session per request). Parsed settings are cached per
# codx_path and invalidated by the file mtime, so a settings save is picked up
# immediately without paying a disk read on the hot path.
_SESSION_SETTINGS_CACHE = {}
_SESSION_SETTINGS_LOCK = threading.Lock()


def _load_cached_settings(codx_path: str):
    """Return ``CODXJuniorSettings`` for *codx_path*, cached by project.json mtime."""
    project_file = os.path.join(codx_path, "project.json")
    try:
        mtime = os.path.getmtime(project_file)
    except OSError:
        return None

    cached = _SESSION_SETTINGS_CACHE.get(codx_path)
    if cached and cached[0] == mtime:
        return cached[1]

    settings = CODXJuniorSettings.from_project_file(project_file)
    with _SESSION_SETTINGS_LOCK:
        _SESSION_SETTINGS_CACHE[codx_path] = (mtime, settings)
    return settings


def get_codx_junior_session(request, codx_path):
    user = get_authenticated_user(request=request)
    sid = request.headers.get("x-sid")
    channel = SessionChannel(sid=sid, sio=sio)
    settings = _load_cached_settings(codx_path) if codx_path else None
    if settings is not None:
        return CODXJuniorSession(settings=settings,
                                  codx_path=codx_path,
                                  channel=channel,
                                  user=user)
    return CODXJuniorSession(codx_path=codx_path, 
                              channel=channel,
                              user=user)

def _attach_session(request: Request, scope) -> None:
    """
    Build the request-scoped ``CODXJuniorSession`` from ``?codx_path``.

    Same contract as the removed middleware: a failure here never breaks the
    request, it only leaves ``request.state.codx_junior_session`` unset.
    """
    codx_path = request.query_params.get("codx_path")
    codx_path = request.headers.get("x-codx-path", codx_path)
    if not codx_path or codx_path in ["undefined", "null"]:
        return
    try:
        session = get_codx_junior_session(request, codx_path)
        scope.setdefault("state", {})["codx_junior_session"] = session
        session.update_last_access_time()
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.error("Error loading settings %s: %s\n%s", codx_path, ex, request.url)


# Paths whose performance is either noise (the log reader itself, static assets,
# the Socket.IO polling transport) or a health probe.
NO_API_LOG_PATHS = ("/api/health",)
NO_API_LOG_PREFIXES = ("/api/static", "/api/socket.io")


class ApiRequestMiddleware:
    """
    Session resolution, timeout, timing and API-call logging in ONE ASGI layer.

    It replaces three stacked ``BaseHTTPMiddleware`` classes. Each of those adds
    an anyio task and a memory-object stream per request and rebuilds the
    request/response stream, which breaks cancellation and corrupted the
    Engine.IO polling transport (``KeyError: 'REQUEST_METHOD'``). A raw ASGI
    middleware keeps the body untouched and adds zero task hops.
    """

    def __init__(self, app):
        self.app = app

    async def __call__(self, scope, receive, send):
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return

        start_time = time.time()
        path = scope.get("path") or ""
        request = Request(scope, receive)

        timeout = GLOBAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
        if path.startswith((BROWSER_LIFECYCLE_PREFIX, COMPUTER_LIFECYCLE_PREFIX)):
            timeout = BROWSER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS

        _attach_session(request, scope)

        status_code = 500
        response_size = 0
        response_started = False
        error_message = None

        async def send_wrapper(message):
            nonlocal status_code, response_started, response_size
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                response_started = True
                status_code = message["status"]
                headers = MutableHeaders(scope=message)
                headers["X-Process-Time"] = str(time.time() - start_time)
                try:
                    response_size = int(headers.get("content-length", 0) or 0)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    response_size = 0
            await send(message)

        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(
                self.app(scope, receive, send_wrapper),
                timeout=timeout,
            )
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            process_time = time.time() - start_time
            error_message = "Request processing time exceeded limit"
            status_code = HTTP_504_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT
            logger.error("HTTP timeout after %.1fs: %s", process_time, request.url)
            if not response_started:
                await JSONResponse(
                    {"detail": "Request processing time exceeded limit",
                     "processing_time": process_time},
                    status_code=HTTP_504_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT,
                )(scope, receive, send)
        except Exception as ex:
            error_message = str(ex) or ex.__class__.__name__
            raise
        finally:
            process_time = time.time() - start_time
            logger.info("Request %s - %d ms", request.url, process_time * 1000)
            if path not in NO_API_LOG_PATHS and not path.startswith(NO_API_LOG_PREFIXES):
                # ``record_api_call`` only enqueues: the write happens off the
                # event loop, so it can never stall other clients again.
                record_api_call(
                    request=request,
                    duration_seconds=process_time,
                    status_code=status_code,
                    error=error_message,
                    response_size=response_size,
                )


app.add_middleware(ApiRequestMiddleware)


# ── Health ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Event-loop lag is the signal that matters for this API: when a synchronous
# call sneaks back into the loop, lag jumps and this probe shows it.
_LAG_SAMPLE_INTERVAL = 0.5
_EVENT_LOOP_LAG = {"last_ms": 0.0, "max_ms": 0.0}
_APP_STARTED_AT = time.time()


async def _event_loop_lag_monitor():  # pragma: no cover - background sampler
    while not APP_STOP_EVENT.is_set():
        started = time.perf_counter()
        try:
            await asyncio.sleep(_LAG_SAMPLE_INTERVAL)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            return
        lag_ms = max(
            0.0,
            (time.perf_counter() - started - _LAG_SAMPLE_INTERVAL) * 1000,
        )
        _EVENT_LOOP_LAG["last_ms"] = round(lag_ms, 1)
        if lag_ms > _EVENT_LOOP_LAG["max_ms"]:
            _EVENT_LOOP_LAG["max_ms"] = round(lag_ms, 1)

@app.get("/api/projects")
def api_find_all_projects(request: Request, user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user)):
    projects = [p for p in list(find_all_user_projects(user)) if is_project_visible(p)]
    workspaces = read_global_settings().workspaces

    user_role = user.role

    def user_has_workspace_access(workspace) -> bool:
        """
        Check if the user has access to the workspace.
        - Admins always have access.
        - If workspace.user_ids is empty, all users have access.
        - Otherwise, only users whose username is in user_ids have access.
        """
        if user_role == "admin":
            return True
        if not workspace.user_ids:
            return True
        return user and user.username in workspace.user_ids

    user_workspaces = [w for w in workspaces \
        if user_has_workspace_access(w) and \
        ("*" in w.project_ids or next((p for p in projects if p.project_id in w.project_ids), None))] 

    if user_role != "admin":
        for workspace in user_workspaces:
            workspace.apps = [app for app in workspace.apps if not app.roles or user_role in app.roles]

    return {
        "projects": projects,
        "workspaces": user_workspaces
    }

"""The JWT/HMAC signing secret must be >= 32 bytes and never a shipped default.

Regression guard for the ``InsecureKeyLengthWarning`` PyJWT logged on every
login: ``GlobalSettings.secret`` used to default to the literal
``"codx-junior-rules"`` — 17 bytes, published in the source tree and therefore
shared by every installation (a token forged on one deployment validated on all
of them). RFC 7518 §3.2 requires at least 32 bytes for HS256.
"""

import json
import warnings

import jwt
import pytest

from codx.junior import global_settings as global_settings_module
from codx.junior.security.secret_key import (
    LEGACY_INSECURE_SECRETS,
    MIN_SECRET_BYTES,
    REASON_LEGACY,
    REASON_MISSING,
    REASON_TOO_SHORT,
    assess_secret,
    generate_secret,
)

LEGACY_PLACEHOLDER = "codx-junior-rules"


def _pyjwt_insecure_warnings(recorded):
    """The PyJWT warnings that motivated this fix (matched by class name)."""
    return [
        record
        for record in recorded
        if type(record.message).__name__ == "InsecureKeyLengthWarning"
    ]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Policy: what may be used to sign tokens
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_generated_secret_is_long_enough():
    secret = generate_secret()
    assert len(secret.encode("utf-8")) >= MIN_SECRET_BYTES
    assert assess_secret(secret).ok


def test_two_generated_secrets_differ():
    assert generate_secret() != generate_secret()


def test_the_old_17_byte_placeholder_is_rejected():
    assessment = assess_secret(LEGACY_PLACEHOLDER)
    assert assessment.byte_length == 17
    assert assessment.legacy
    assert not assessment.ok
    assert assessment.reason == REASON_LEGACY
    # Never log the secret itself, only its fingerprint.
    assert LEGACY_PLACEHOLDER not in assessment.describe()
    for legacy in LEGACY_INSECURE_SECRETS:
        assert not assess_secret(legacy).ok


def test_missing_secret_is_rejected():
    for empty in (None, ""):
        assessment = assess_secret(empty)
        assert not assessment.ok
        assert assessment.reason == REASON_MISSING


def test_short_secret_is_rejected():
    assessment = assess_secret("x" * (MIN_SECRET_BYTES - 1))
    assert not assessment.ok
    assert assessment.reason == REASON_TOO_SHORT


def test_minimum_length_secret_is_accepted():
    assert assess_secret("x" * MIN_SECRET_BYTES).ok


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The warning itself
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_generated_secret_does_not_trigger_pyjwt_warning():
    secret = generate_secret()
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as recorded:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        token = jwt.encode({"username": "admin"}, secret, algorithm="HS256")
        assert jwt.decode(token, secret, algorithms=["HS256"])["username"] == "admin"
    assert _pyjwt_insecure_warnings(recorded) == []


def test_legacy_placeholder_triggers_pyjwt_warning():
    """The premise of the fix: PyJWT warns on the old 17-byte default."""
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as recorded:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        jwt.encode({"username": "admin"}, LEGACY_PLACEHOLDER, algorithm="HS256")
    assert _pyjwt_insecure_warnings(recorded)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Migration / startup behaviour (isolated settings store)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.fixture()
def isolated_settings(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Settings store in a temporary folder, seeded with the legacy secret."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("CODX_JUNIOR_CONFIG_FOLDER", str(tmp_path))
    monkeypatch.setattr(global_settings_module, "_manager", None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(global_settings_module, "_GLOBAL_SETTINGS_CACHE", None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(global_settings_module, "_GLOBAL_SETTINGS_CACHED_AT", 0.0)
    monkeypatch.setattr(global_settings_module, "GLOBAL_SETTINGS", None)
    manager = global_settings_module.get_manager()
    manager.write_section("secret", LEGACY_PLACEHOLDER)
    global_settings_module.invalidate_global_settings_cache()
    return manager


def _stored_secret(manager):
    return json.loads(
        (manager.settings_dir / "secret.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    )


def test_ensure_signing_secret_replaces_and_persists_the_placeholder(isolated_settings):
    secret = global_settings_module.ensure_signing_secret(
        persist=True, raise_on_persist_failure=True
    )

    assert assess_secret(secret).ok
    assert _stored_secret(isolated_settings) == secret
    # Idempotent: a stored secret is reused, never rotated on every call.
    assert global_settings_module.ensure_signing_secret(persist=True) == secret


def test_ensure_signing_secret_updates_the_caller_snapshot(isolated_settings):
    """A long-lived settings snapshot (UserSecurityManager) must not stay weak."""
    settings = global_settings_module.read_global_settings(refresh=True)
    assert not assess_secret(settings.secret).ok

    secret = global_settings_module.ensure_signing_secret(
        settings=settings, persist=True
    )

    assert settings.secret == secret
    assert assess_secret(settings.secret).ok
    assert global_settings_module.ensure_signing_secret(settings=settings) == secret


def test_write_global_settings_never_persists_a_placeholder(isolated_settings):
    """Saving all sections used to write the default secret back to disk."""
    settings = global_settings_module.read_global_settings(refresh=True)
    settings.secret = LEGACY_PLACEHOLDER

    global_settings_module.write_global_settings(settings)

    stored = _stored_secret(isolated_settings)
    assert assess_secret(stored).ok
    assert stored == settings.secret


def test_validate_signing_secret_at_startup_returns_a_usable_secret(isolated_settings):
    secret = global_settings_module.validate_signing_secret_at_startup()

    assert assess_secret(secret).ok
    assert _stored_secret(isolated_settings) == secret
